text:
Case: United India Insurance Company Ltd vs Neelam Devi And Others
Court: High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh (2023)
Legal area: motor_accident; stage: appeal
Issues: driving_license_validity, license_breach_defence, insurance_liability, policy_breach, pay_and_recover, compensation_quantum, compensation_enhancement, future_prospects, income_determination, consortium, section_166
Vehicles: tanker, truck, car
Stance: claimant_supporting, insurer_supporting, mixed
Facts: On 21.11.2013 at about 10:00 P.M., Munish Kumar and friends Ram Niwas, Sultan and Sunil were travelling from Narwana to Vrindavan in a Maruti Car (HR-99-QMTP-3245) which was struck by a Truck/Tanker (HR-38-F-4365), causing deaths of Munish Kumar, Sultan Singh and Ram Niwas and injuries to Sunil. FIR No. 938 dated 22.11.2013 was registered under Sections 279, 337, 338 and 304-A IPC at Police Station City Jind. The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jind passed a common award dated 30.10.2017 awarding compensation in four MACP cases totalling over Rs. 38 lacs. United India Insurance Company filed four appeals (FAOs 1113, 1114, 1119, 1120 of 2018) challenging the award. Driver Sandeep's license (Ex.R-2) was valid for MC, LMV, HGV, HTV but lacked the special endorsement required under Rule 9 of Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 for driving a vehicle carrying dangerous or hazardous goods. Claimants in FAO-1119-2018 filed cross-objections seeking enhancement of compensation for death of Munish Kumar, supported by Income Tax Returns showing gross annual income of Rs. 2,40,380/-. Insurer challenged income assessment at DC Rate instead of Minimum Wages Act and questioned awards for consortium and funeral expenses.
Holdings: A driver of a vehicle carrying dangerous or hazardous goods requires a special endorsement on the driving license under Rule 9 of Central Motor Vehicles Rule, 1989; absence of such endorsement is a breach of insurance policy conditions. Despite the policy breach, the insurer cannot escape liability to third-party claimants and must pay compensation, retaining the right to recover from the insured. There is no fixed rule that the income of a deceased must be assessed only as per minimum wages; the facts and circumstances of each case must be evaluated. Future prospects must be added to income for compensation calculation as mandated by National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others.
Outcome: Four appeals by the insurer partly allowed. Driver Sandeep found to lack the special endorsement required for driving a Tanker carrying hazardous goods under Rule 9 of Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, constituting a policy breach; Tribunal findings on Issue No. 3 reversed giving insurer the right to recover from the insured. Insurer nonetheless directed to pay compensation. Compensation recalculated upward in FAO-1114-2018 and FAO-1119-2018 with 40% future prospects applied; cross-objections in FAO-1119-2018 accepted, compensation for Munish Kumar's death enhanced to Rs. 40,60,400/-. All four appeals and cross-objections disposed of.
United India Insurance Company filed four appeals challenging a common award dated 30.10.2017 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jind, arising from a motor vehicle accident on 21.11.2013 in which a Truck/Tanker struck a Maruti Car, resulting in three deaths and one injury. The insurer contested the quantum of compensation and the validity of driver Sandeep's license for operating a Tanker transporting hazardous goods. The High Court upheld the income assessment method (rejecting the insurer's plea to restrict income to Minimum Wages Act) and applied 40% future prospects for the 22-year-old and 32-year-old deceased, and 25% for the 46-year-old deceased, as mandated by National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi. On the license issue, the court reversed the Tribunal and held that a special endorsement under Rule 9 of Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 is required for driving a vehicle carrying dangerous or hazardous goods, which Sandeep lacked, constituting a policy breach. Nonetheless, the insurer was directed to pay the compensation with the right to recover from the insured. The cross-objections filed by claimants in FAO-1119-2018 were accepted and compensation for the death of Munish Kumar was substantially enhanced to Rs. 40,60,400/-. All four appeals and cross-objections were disposed of.

Case: Liyakat Ali vs Smt Chunni Devi
Court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (2010)
Legal area: motor_accident; stage: appeal
Issues: insurance_liability, policy_breach, third_party_liability, owner_liability, permit_violation, section_166
Vehicles: tractor, trailer
Stance: insurer_supporting, adverse_to_claimant
Facts: On 02.12.2000, deceased Arvind Kumar was travelling on a scooter when Tractor No. UP-35-B-1649 took a sharp turn and iron rods loaded in the trolley/trailer attached to the tractor struck him; he died on the spot. The tractor was insured but the trolley/trailer was not separately insured; no premium was paid for the trolley. The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Unnao awarded Rs. 1,18,850/- against the owner of the tractor (Liyakat Ali), holding the insurer not liable. The tractor was insured only for agricultural use; at the time of accident it was carrying bricks and iron rods for construction of a room (pakki boring), not for agricultural purposes. The owner admitted in paragraph 3 of his affidavit that the trolley was being used to carry iron rods and bricks for construction purposes.
Holdings: A trailer/trolley attached to a tractor is part of the tractor and need not be separately insured under Section 146 of the Motor Vehicles Act; if the prime mover (tractor) is insured and the driver's negligence is established, the insurer cannot escape liability merely because the trailer was not separately insured. However, where the tractor was insured only for agricultural use and was being used for a non-agricultural purpose at the time of the accident, there is a breach of insurance policy conditions and the insurer is not liable; the owner must pay compensation.
Outcome: Appeal dismissed for different reasons. While the court held that a trailer/trolley attached to a tractor is part of the tractor and covered by the tractor's insurance (not requiring separate premium), it found that the tractor was insured only for agricultural use and was carrying bricks and iron rods for construction — a non-agricultural purpose — constituting a breach of policy conditions. The insurer was therefore not liable and the owner of the tractor was held liable to pay the compensation of Rs. 1,18,850/-.
An appeal by the owner of a tractor (Liyakat Ali) against an award of Rs. 1,18,850/- by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Unnao, arising from the death of Arvind Kumar on 02.12.2000 when iron rods in the trolley attached to the tractor struck him as the tractor took a sharp turn near Hyderabad Paisara. The tractor was insured but the trolley was not separately insured. The court held that a trailer/trolley is part of the tractor and covered under the tractor's insurance, so the insurer could not escape liability merely for want of separate trailer insurance. However, the critical finding was that the tractor was insured only for agricultural use and was actually carrying bricks and iron rods for construction of a room — a non-agricultural purpose — constituting a breach of insurance policy conditions. Accordingly, the insurer was held not liable and the award was upheld against the owner of the tractor. The appeal was dismissed.

Case: United India Insurance Co Ltd vs Smt Parvathi Hebbar W/O Late Ramakrishna Hebbar
Court: High Court of Karnataka at Bengaluru (2017)
Legal area: motor_accident; stage: appeal
Issues: driving_license_validity, license_breach_defence, insurance_liability, policy_breach, pay_and_recover, third_party_liability, compensation_quantum, section_166
Vehicles: car
Stance: insurer_supporting, adverse_to_claimant
Facts: On 02-07-2008 at about 6.30 a.m., deceased Ramakrishna Hebbar was standing on the southern side mud portion of Udupi-Karkala Road when the driver of Maruthi Omni (KA-20/Z-3931) drove rashly and dashed against him; he succumbed to injuries on 16-07-2008. The deceased was aged about 60 years and working as a Head Cook earning Rs. 15,000/- per month. Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kundapura awarded Rs. 2,45,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. fastening liability on the insurer. The driving license of the driver of the Maruthi Omni had expired on 30-04-2008 (more than 30 days before the accident on 02-07-2008) and was renewed only on 04-07-2008, after the accident. The insurer proved through evidence that as on the date of accident, the driver of offending Maruthi Omni was not holding a valid and effective driving license.
Holdings: Where a driving license has expired and an application for renewal is made more than 30 days after expiry, the proviso to Section 15(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act applies and the license is renewed only from the date of renewal, not from the date of expiry; hence the driver cannot be deemed to hold a valid license on the date of the accident. Despite the policy breach, the insurer must pay the awarded compensation to the claimants (as third parties have a statutory right to recover) and then recover the same from the insured, applying the pay-and-recover principle.
Outcome: Appeal allowed. Liability shifted from insurer to owner. The driving license expired on 30-04-2008 and the accident occurred on 02-07-2008; since renewal was applied for more than 30 days after expiry, the proviso to Section 15(1) operates and the license is valid only from the date of renewal (04-07-2008), not retrospectively. The driver was not holding a valid license on the date of the accident, constituting a policy breach. However, since third parties have a statutory right to recover compensation, the insurer was directed to pay the awarded sum and recover from the insured by applying the pay-and-recover principle.
United India Insurance Company challenged the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kundapura's award of Rs. 2,45,000/- for the death of Ramakrishna Hebbar who was struck by a Maruthi Omni on 02-07-2008. The key dispute was whether the insurer was liable when the driver's license had expired on 30-04-2008 — more than 30 days before the accident — and was renewed only on 04-07-2008. The Karnataka High Court held that under the proviso to Section 15(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, where renewal is applied for more than 30 days after expiry, the license is renewed only from the date of renewal, not retrospectively from the date of expiry. Since the accident fell in the interregnum period when the driver lacked a valid license, there was a breach of policy conditions. The court reversed the Tribunal's finding and fastened liability on the owner. However, since it is the statutory right of third parties to recover compensation, the insurer was directed to pay the awarded compensation and then recover from the insured, applying the pay-and-recover principle established in National Insurance Company v. Swaran Singh and Manuara Khatun v. Rajesh Kr. Singh.

Case: Oriental Insurance Company vs Soma Devi and Others
Court: High Court of Himachal Pradesh at Shimla (2020)
Legal area: motor_accident; stage: appeal
Issues: rash_negligent_driving, negligence_proof, fir_credibility, insurance_liability, compensation_quantum, compensation_enhancement, future_prospects, income_determination, just_compensation, section_166
Vehicles: motorcycle, car
Stance: claimant_supporting, adverse_to_insurer
Facts: On Jun 19, 2010, deceased Harish Kumar (aged 21 years, born Jan 21, 1989) was riding a motorcycle (HP34A-9526) when it collided with a car (HP33B-2444) driven by Jai Ram near Bhangrotu Bridge; both riders of the motorcycle fell and sustained injuries; Harish Kumar died while being transported to IGMC Hospital Shimla. FIR No. 219 dated Jun 20, 2010 was registered by Jai Ram (driver of the car) at Police Station-Balh, District Mandi, HP, alleging rash and negligent driving by the deceased motorcycle rider. The mother Soma Devi filed a Claim Petition under Section 166 of MV Act claiming Rs. 15 lacs; she alleged her son earned Rs. 10,000/- per month working in M/s Sidharth Communications. Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (1), Mandi, HP, vide award dated Aug 31, 2012 awarded total compensation of Rs. 4,00,000/- fastening liability on Oriental Insurance Company, treating income as Rs. 3,500/- per month (unskilled worker). Oriental Insurance Company challenged the award arguing the car's driver Jai Ram was not at fault and the FIR was against the deceased motorcycle rider.
Holdings: A FIR recording a one-sided version from the surviving car driver, without corroboration or investigation of other eyewitnesses, cannot be accepted as conclusive proof of negligence by the deceased motorcycle rider. Under Order 41 Rule 33 CPC and Section 168 MV Act, courts may enhance compensation beyond the amount claimed or awarded even in the absence of cross-objections, where the award is manifestly unjust to a poor claimant. For a self-employed bachelor below 40 years, 40% future prospects applies (Pranay Sethi), 50% is deducted for personal expenses, and multiplier 18 applies for age 21-25 years (Sarla Verma).
Outcome: Appeal disposed of. Insurer's contention that the car's driver was not at fault was rejected; the FIR was found to be a one-sided version from the car driver, without independent investigation of the surviving occupant. Insurer's liability affirmed. Compensation enhanced from Rs. 4,00,000/- to Rs. 5,99,000/- by applying 40% future prospects on Rs. 3,500/- (self-employed, below 40 years per Pranay Sethi), 50% deduction for personal expenses (bachelor), multiplier 18 for age group 21-25 years (Sarla Verma), plus conventional heads: loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-, consortium Rs. 40,000/-, funeral expenses Rs. 15,000/-. Interest reduced from 7.5% to 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition.
Oriental Insurance Company challenged the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mandi's award of Rs. 4,00,000/- for the death of Harish Kumar (aged 21 years) in a road accident on Jun 19, 2010, in which his motorcycle collided with an insured car driven by Jai Ram. The FIR was registered against the deceased based on the car driver's version, and the police investigation concluded that the motorcycle was rash and negligent. The Himachal Pradesh High Court found the FIR to be a one-sided version from the surviving car driver; the joint reply filed by the car owner and driver in the claim petition contained an improvement over the FIR, undermining its credibility. The court affirmed liability on the insurer. Applying National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi, the court calculated just compensation: 40% future prospects on Rs. 3,500/-, 50% personal expense deduction (bachelor), multiplier 18 for age 21, plus conventional heads as per Pranay Sethi. Total compensation was enhanced to Rs. 5,99,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of filing the petition.

text:
Case: L And T Insurance Co Ltd vs Bindudevi Samharu Yadav And Others
Court: High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad (2026)
Legal area: motor_accident; stage: appeal
Issues: fake_license, license_breach_defence, insurance_liability, maintainability, workmens_compensation, section_166, section_167_mv_act, third_party_liability
Vehicles: tempo, dumper
Stance: claimant_supporting, adverse_to_insurer
Facts: On 19.05.2013 at about 1:00 p.m., deceased Sunil Samharu Yadav (aged 28 years, driver of tempo DN-09-K-9486 loaded with yarn) parked his tempo on the left side of National Highway No. 8 to change a punctured tyre; a dumper truck (GJ-18-X-9452) driven rashly by respondent No. 5 struck the tempo from behind, causing fatal injuries. Claimants filed proceedings before the Workmen's Compensation Commissioner against the employer of the deceased and the insurer of the tempo (ICICI Lombard) and received compensation of Rs. 8,39,680/-. Claimants also filed a claim petition under Section 166 of MV Act before Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxiliary), Navsari against the driver, owner and insurer (L&T Insurance) of the offending dumper truck. Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Navsari awarded Rs. 12,12,400/- with interest at 9% p.a. from the date of filing of claim petition till realization. L&T Insurance challenged the award on two grounds: (1) bar of Section 167 MV Act due to prior Workmen's Compensation proceedings; and (2) that the driver of the dumper truck was holding a fake driving license.
Holdings: Section 167 of the Motor Vehicles Act bars dual proceedings only where the claimants seek compensation from the same employer/tortfeasor before both forums; where the parties before each forum are entirely different, the bar of Section 167 does not apply. The liability under the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 is the statutory liability of the employer while the liability under Section 166 of the MV Act is tortious liability; claims against different parties under different instruments are not barred. The insurer bears the burden of proving by cogent documentary evidence that the driving license was fake; mere oral evidence of its own legal officer without proper RTO documentation fails to discharge this burden.
Outcome: Appeal dismissed. The bar of Section 167 of MV Act does not apply because the parties before the Workmen's Compensation Commissioner (employer of the deceased and ICICI Lombard as insurer of the tempo) and the parties before the MACT (driver, owner and L&T Insurance as insurer of the dumper truck) were entirely different; the two claims arose under different legal relationships. On the driving license issue, the insurer failed to prove by cogent evidence that the license was fake; merely relying on oral testimony of a legal officer without producing proper documentation from the RTO was insufficient. Award of Rs. 12,12,400/- maintained.
L&T Insurance Company appealed against a MACT award of Rs. 12,12,400/- arising from the death of Sunil Samharu Yadav (aged 28 years) on 19.05.2013 when a dumper truck struck his parked tempo while he was changing a punctured tyre on NH-8. The insurer raised two defenses: (1) Section 167 MV Act bars the claim since claimants had already received Rs. 8,39,680/- from the employer under the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923; and (2) the dumper driver held a fake driving license. The Gujarat High Court dismissed both defenses. On Section 167, it held that the bar applies only where the claimants seek compensation from the same tortfeasor/employer in both forums; here, the Workmen's Compensation proceedings were against the employer (and ICICI Lombard as insurer of the tempo) while the MACT proceedings were against the tortfeasors (dumper truck driver, owner, and L&T Insurance) — different parties with different liabilities. On the fake license, the insurer failed to lead cogent documentary evidence to prove the license was fake; mere oral testimony of the legal officer was insufficient. The appeal was dismissed and the award maintained.

text:
Case: National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Smt. Meena And 4 Others
Court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench (2024)
Legal area: motor_accident; stage: appeal
Issues: contributory_negligence, negligence_proof, driving_license_validity, license_breach_defence, pay_and_recover, insurance_liability, compensation_quantum, compensation_enhancement, future_prospects, income_determination, section_166
Vehicles: tanker
Stance: claimant_supporting, adverse_to_insurer
Facts: On 12.5.2006 at about 7.00 A.M., deceased Sundar Lal was riding a moped (UP-32-AB/8094) near Neelam Traders, Devpur Tara, Police Station Talkatora, Lucknow when a Tanker (UP32-T/6251) driven negligently collided with the moped; Sundar Lal died on 15.5.2006. The deceased was a government servant with a monthly salary of Rs. 8,841/-; the MACT deducted Rs. 500/- towards VPF and Rs. 150/- towards festival advance while calculating income. Eye-witness P.W.-2 (Ram Gopal, also riding a moped) testified that deceased was on the left side of the road, took further left to avoid the Tanker, and was not negligent. The MACT applied 50% contributory negligence based on the police site plan (relied upon as showing head-on collision), awarding only 50% of the calculated compensation. Valid driving license of the Tanker driver was not produced; MACT directed insurer to pay compensation with right to recover from the owner. MACT awarded Rs. 4,26,880/- with 6% simple interest; two appeals filed: F.A.F.O. 123/2012 by claimants and F.A.F.O. 148/2012 by the insurer.
Holdings: Where there is consistent and credible testimony of an eye-witness that the deceased was not negligent, the Tribunal cannot discard that testimony and apply contributory negligence solely on the basis of a police site plan that does not clearly indicate a head-on collision. Even where the driver of the offending vehicle does not possess a valid driving license, the insurer is liable to pay compensation to claimants and has a right to recover from the insured; this follows S. Iyyapan v. M/s. United India Insurance Company. VPF contributions and festival advances form part of the deceased's gross income and cannot be deducted while calculating income available to dependent family members. For a government servant aged between 40 and 50 years, 30% must be added to income towards future prospects as mandated by National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi.
Outcome: Insurer's appeal (F.A.F.O. 148/2012) dismissed: following S. Iyyapan v. United India Insurance Company, even where the driver lacks a valid license, the insurer must pay compensation to claimants with right to recover from the owner. Claimants' appeal (F.A.F.O. 123/2012) partly allowed: 50% contributory negligence finding reversed; 100% negligence attributed to Tanker driver based on credible unrebutted eye-witness testimony; VPF and festival advance deductions restored to income; 30% future prospects added; interest increased from 6% to 7%; total compensation recalculated to Rs. 13,74,876/-; insurer directed to pay with right to recover from owner Anil Kumar Gupta.
Two cross-appeals arose from the MACT award in M.A.C.P. No. 190 of 2009 relating to the death of Sundar Lal (a government servant) on 12.5.2006 when a Tanker collided with his moped in Lucknow. The MACT applied 50% contributory negligence based on a site plan and directed the insurer to pay with right to recover, as the Tanker driver's license was not produced. The Allahabad High Court (Lucknow Bench) dismissed the insurer's appeal: following S. Iyyapan, the insurer must pay even where the driver lacks a valid license, with a right to recover from the owner. The claimants' appeal was partly allowed: the 50% contributory negligence finding was reversed since eye-witness P.W.-2 gave consistent and unrebutted testimony that the deceased was on the left side of the road, and the site plan did not clearly indicate head-on collision. VPF and festival advance deductions were reversed; 30% future prospects added for the government servant aged 40-50; interest enhanced from 6% to 7%. Total compensation was enhanced from Rs. 4,26,880/- to Rs. 13,74,876/-.

text:
Case: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Harpreet Singh and Others
Court: High Court of Jammu and Kashmir at Jammu (2014)
Legal area: motor_accident; stage: appeal
Issues: loss_of_dependency, compensation_quantum, compensation_reduction, income_determination, multiplier, section_166
Vehicles: car
Stance: insurer_supporting, adverse_to_claimant
Facts: On 29.09.2007, deceased Amarjeet Singh was travelling from Kishtwar to Jammu in a car (JK02D-9212) owned and driven by Inderjit Singh Bali; the car met with an accident near Thathri, plunged into a trench, and Amarjeet Singh died. The deceased was a Government servant serving as Manager QC in the Food Corporation of India with a monthly salary of Rs. 24,149/-; he was aged 54 years at the time of death. Claimants Harpreet Singh (son, employed as clerk in Doordarshan, Central Government service) and Harbaksh Singh (son, MBA student) filed claim under Section 166 MV Act. Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jammu awarded Rs. 17,53,800/- treating family strength as 3 (deceased + 2 sons) with 1/3 deduction for personal expenses, multiplier 9. Insurer challenged: Harpreet Singh being gainfully employed in Central Government service is not dependent on the deceased and should not be counted for loss of dependency; only Harbaksh Singh (MBA student) qualifies as a dependent.
Holdings: A legal representative of a motor accident victim who was not financially dependent on the deceased at the time of death is not entitled to compensation under the head 'loss of dependency'; such a claimant is entitled only to compensation for loss to estate and the statutory minimum under Section 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act. For calculating 'loss of dependency', only financially dependent claimants are counted to determine family strength and the applicable personal expense deduction; non-dependent legal representatives are excluded from this computation. Where the deceased was above 50 years of age at the time of death, no addition to income on account of future prospects is warranted under Sarla Verma.
Outcome: Appeal allowed in part. Claimant Harpreet Singh, being gainfully employed as a clerk in Doordarshan (Central Government service) and not dependent on the deceased at the time of death, is not entitled to compensation under the head 'loss of dependency'; he is entitled only to compensation for loss to estate and the statutory minimum under Section 140. Family strength recalculated as 2 (deceased + Harbaksh Singh only); 50% deduction for personal expenses; no addition for future prospects (deceased above 50 years); income tax of Rs. 15,000/- deducted from gross income. Multiplier 9 (correctly scaled down from applicable 11). Compensation under loss of dependency: Rs. 12,36,600/-, plus Rs. 15,000/- funeral expenses. Total Rs. 12,51,600/- (reduced from Rs. 17,53,800/-).
National Insurance Company appealed against the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jammu's award of Rs. 17,53,800/- for the death of Amarjeet Singh (54-year-old FCI Manager, salary Rs. 24,149/- per month) who died in a road accident on 29.09.2007. The insurer challenged the treatment of both sons as dependants when Harpreet Singh was admittedly employed as a clerk in Doordarshan (Central Government service). The High Court of Jammu and Kashmir allowed the appeal in part. Relying on Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, U.P. State Road Transport Corporation v. Trilok Chandra, and Smt. Manjuri Bera v. Oriental Insurance Company, the court held that only financially dependent legal representatives are entitled to compensation under 'loss of dependency'. Harpreet Singh, being gainfully employed in Central Government service, was excluded from this head and entitled only to loss to estate and the statutory minimum under Section 140. Family strength was recalculated as 2 (deceased + Harbaksh Singh), with 50% deduction for personal expenses; income tax of Rs. 15,000/- deducted; no future prospects addition (deceased above 50 years); multiplier correctly reduced to 9. Total compensation reduced to Rs. 12,51,600/-.

text:
Case: General Manager Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation vs Khatujabee
Court: High Court of Karnataka (Full Bench) (1990)
Legal area: motor_accident; stage: appeal
Issues: multiplier, loss_of_dependency, compensation_quantum, just_compensation, income_determination
Stance: neutral
Facts: Fatal motor accident involving Kashimsab (Blacksmith, aged 40) whose dependants claimed compensation before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal Tribunal awarded Rs. 2,70,000 under 'loss of dependency' using multiplier of 30; appeal confirmed award with 20% deduction for life's uncertainties Division Bench in Khatujabee's case (MFA 708/1990) held that the operative multiplier principle in Bhandary's case had ceased to be binding after SC decisions in Jyotsna Dey and Rajendra Kumari under Art. 141 A second Division Bench referred the question of whether Bhandary's case stood impliedly overruled to the Full Bench Full Bench examined nature of ratio decidendi and binding precedent under Art. 141 with reference to multiple SC decisions
Holdings: The 'operative multiplier' principle elaborated in Bhandary's case constitutes law declared by the Karnataka High Court and is a binding precedent for Tribunals in the State. SC decisions in Jyotsna Dey and Rajendra Kumari contain fact-specific conclusions reached in the setting of the particular cases before them and do not constitute 'law declared' under Art. 141 on the general question of multiplier selection. A decision is binding as a precedent only with respect to the ratio or principle laid down therein, not because of its conclusion; an obiter cannot take the place of the ratio.
Outcome: Full Bench answered that H.T. Bhandary v. Muniyamma [ILR 1985(2) Karnataka 2337] does NOT stand overruled by the SC decisions in Rajendra Kumari v. Shanta Trivedi and Jyotsna Dey v. State of Assam [1987(1) ACJ 172]. The contrary view taken by the Division Bench in Khatujabee's case stands overruled. The operative multiplier principle (base multiplier 16, scaled down with age) remains binding on all Motor Accident Claims Tribunals in Karnataka.
This 1990 Karnataka High Court Full Bench judgment resolved a reference question on whether the 'operative multiplier' principle established in H.T. Bhandary v. Muniyamma (ILR 1985(2) Karnataka 2337) was impliedly overruled by Supreme Court decisions in Jyotsna Dey v. State of Assam (1987 1 ACJ 172) and Rajendra Kumari v. Shanta Trivedi. The reference arose from a Division Bench in MFA No. 708/1990 where KSRTC appealed a Tribunal award applying a multiplier of 30 for a fatal accident involving a blacksmith. The Full Bench extensively examined the nature of binding precedent under Article 141 of the Constitution, holding that a Supreme Court decision is 'law declared' only with respect to the ratio and principle laid down therein—not mere conclusions reached on specific facts. Applying this test, the Full Bench found that the multiplier choices in Jyotsna Dey and Rajendra Kumari were factual determinations rather than legal principles of general application. Since those decisions laid down no general rule on multiplier selection, they could not have impliedly overruled Bhandary's carefully elaborated operative multiplier principle, which capped the base multiplier at 16 and provided a systematic framework for scaling it down with the deceased's age. The Full Bench answered the reference in favour of Bhandary's case and overruled the contrary view in Khatujabee's case.

Case: Kamal S/o Shiv Ram vs Mursleem S/o Mohd. Akil and Others
Court: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Pilot Court), Karkardooma Courts, Delhi (2019)
Legal area: motor_accident; stage: claim_petition
Issues: rash_negligent_driving, contributory_negligence, driving_license_validity, compensation_quantum, income_determination, section_166, just_compensation, interest_on_compensation
Vehicles: motorcycle
Stance: mixed
Facts: On 31.08.2018 at about 20:00 hrs at 4th Pushta, Sonia Vihar, Delhi, the offending vehicle DL 1 LX 2320 driven rashly and negligently hit the motorcycle of injured Kamal FIR No. 188/18 was registered at PS Sonia Vihar; three petitioners—Kamal (rider), Rajni (pillion, minor aged 14), and Tannu (pillion, minor aged 13)—were injured Kamal admitted in cross-examination that he had no driving licence at the time of the accident and all three were not wearing helmets Income of Kamal assessed at Rs. 13,896/month (minimum wages for unskilled worker as on 31.08.2018); Rajni and Tannu were students with no independent income Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. insured the offending vehicle; no policy violation found by respondents
Holdings: Negligence of the respondent driver is established on the standard of preponderance of probability through the FIR, site plan, and medical records; no rebuttal evidence was led by the respondents. Contributory negligence of 50% is applicable where the motorcycle rider had no driving licence and none of the three occupants wore helmets. Income of a claimant with no documentary proof of earnings is assessed at the minimum wages applicable on the date of accident.
Outcome: All three DAR petitions (402/18, 403/18, 404/18) allowed with 50% deduction for contributory negligence. Kamal awarded Rs. 55,844 (reduced from Rs. 1,11,688); Rajni and Tannu each awarded Rs. 48,500 (reduced from Rs. 97,000 each). Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. directed to pay all amounts within one month with 9% per annum interest from date of filing of each petition.
This award disposed of three connected DAR petitions (402/18, 403/18, 404/18) filed before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi by Kamal, Rajni, and Tannu—all injured on 31 August 2018 when their motorcycle was struck by rashly driven vehicle DL 1 LX 2320 at 4th Pushta, Sonia Vihar. FIR No. 188/18 was registered at PS Sonia Vihar. Negligence of the driver was established on the standard of preponderance of probability through the FIR, site plan, and MLC records; the respondents led no counter-evidence. The central issue was contributory negligence: Kamal (the motorcycle rider) admitted in cross-examination that he had no driving licence and that none of the three occupants were wearing helmets. The Tribunal accordingly deducted 50% of the gross award from each claimant for contributory negligence. Kamal was awarded Rs. 1,11,688 gross (primarily loss of wages for three months at minimum wages of Rs. 13,896 per month, plus pain and suffering, attendant charges, and diet), reduced to Rs. 55,844. Rajni (aged 14, student) and Tannu (aged 13, student) each received Rs. 97,000 gross (primarily pain and suffering and medical incidentals), reduced to Rs. 48,500. Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co., insurer of the offending vehicle, was held liable to pay all three reduced amounts with 9% per annum interest from the date of filing.

Case: Raju Gupta S/o Sh. Madan Mohan Gupta vs Manoj Kumar and Others
Court: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Pilot Court), Karkardooma Courts, Delhi (2018)
Legal area: motor_accident; stage: claim_petition
Issues: rash_negligent_driving, compensation_quantum, income_determination, section_166, future_prospects, just_compensation, interest_on_compensation, insurance_liability
Vehicles: auto_rickshaw, truck
Stance: claimant_supporting
Facts: On 14/15.02.2016 at about 2 AM, all three petitioners boarded auto-rickshaw DL 1 RM 0893 at Khajuri Chowk to go to Sonia Vihar; driver drove rashly at high speed and collided with stationary truck HR 55F 2507 at Wazirabad Road in front of Sonia Vihar Water Plant FIR No. 155/16 was registered at PS Kajoori Khas under Sections 279/337/338 IPC; respondents were common across all three petitions Raju Gupta (DAR 153/16) sustained 37% physical disability in left lower limb and right upper limb; functional disability assessed at 20% of the whole body Income assessed at minimum wages for unskilled workman on 15.02.2016 at Rs. 9,178 per month; no future prospects addition per Pranay Sethi judgment Neelam (DAR 154/16) and Satish Kumar (DAR 155/16) sustained simple injuries only; no significant loss of income or disability established National Insurance Co. held liable under a valid policy (No. 361801/31/14/670000152) covering the offending auto for the period 10.03.2015 to 09.03.2016
Holdings: Negligence of the driver is established through FIR, site plan, and eyewitness evidence on preponderance of probability; denial without counter-evidence is insufficient to rebut the claim. Functional disability for compensation purposes is assessed as a percentage of the whole body even where the physical disability certificate specifies injury to a particular limb, following Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar (2011) 1 SCC 343. Future prospects cannot be added to income assessed at statutory minimum wages where the petitioner has not proved a fixed salary or regular employment.
Outcome: All three petitions allowed. Raju Gupta (DAR 153/16) awarded Rs. 5,33,033 (primarily Rs. 3,52,432 for future loss of income at 20% functional disability, multiplier 16, plus wages for 5 months, pain and suffering, amenities, attendant charges, and medical expenses). Neelam (DAR 154/16) and Satish Kumar (DAR 155/16) each awarded Rs. 15,000 for simple injuries. National Insurance Co. directed to pay all amounts with 9% interest from date of filing.
This common award disposed of three DAR petitions (153/16, 154/16, 155/16) before the MACT, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi. On 14-15 February 2016 at 2 AM, the three petitioners—Raju Gupta, Neelam, and Satish Kumar—were passengers in auto-rickshaw DL 1 RM 0893. The driver drove rashly at high speed, causing the auto to collide with a stationary truck (HR 55F 2507) at Wazirabad Road. FIR No. 155/16 was registered under Sections 279/337/338 IPC. Negligence was established via FIR, site plan, and MLC records; respondents produced no controverting witnesses. For DAR 153/16 (Raju Gupta): a disability certificate established 37% physical disability in left lower limb and right upper limb; the Tribunal assessed 20% functional disability following Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar (2011) 1 SCC 343. Income was assessed at minimum wages for unskilled workman (Rs. 9,178 per month as of 15.02.2016); no future prospects were added per Pranay Sethi. Future loss of earnings was Rs. 3,52,432 (income × 12 × multiplier 16 × 20%), with additional awards for wages (5 months), pain and suffering, amenities, medical bills, conveyance, and attendant charges totalling Rs. 5,33,033. Neelam (154/16) and Satish Kumar (155/16) sustained simple injuries and were awarded Rs. 15,000 each. National Insurance Co. held liable for all three awards with 9% interest per annum from date of filing.

Case: Asfaq Ahmad and Others vs Satender and Others
Court: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Pilot Court), Karkardooma Courts, Delhi (2018)
Legal area: motor_accident; stage: claim_petition
Issues: rash_negligent_driving, loss_of_dependency, compensation_quantum, income_determination, section_166, multiplier, future_prospects, just_compensation, interest_on_compensation
Vehicles: motorcycle, bus
Stance: claimant_supporting
Facts: On 10.02.2018 at about 5 PM, deceased Istkhar (approximately 27-28 years, bachelor) and injured Sherddin were travelling on motorcycle DL 1 SZ 1427; bus UP 15 AT 4990 driven rashly by Satender struck the motorcycle near village Meetlli towards Meerut Istkhar was brought dead to Baghpat Hospital; Crime No. 166/18 was registered at PS Baghpat under Sections 279/337/427/304-A IPC; chargesheet was filed Istkhar's income assessed at minimum wages for a matriculate (Rs. 11,830 per month as on 10.02.2018); 50% deduction applied as he was a bachelor; multiplier 17 applied for age approximately 28; no future prospects awarded per Laxmidhar Nayak Loss of dependency: Rs. 12,06,660; total MACT 74/18 award: Rs. 12,36,660 (including loss of estate Rs. 15,000 and funeral expenses Rs. 15,000) Sherddin (MACT 124/18): injuries proved but no disability established (treating doctor not summoned); no future loss of income; total award Rs. 1,89,150 Oriental Insurance Co. held liable under policy No. 252405/31/2018/5376 (covering the bus from 30.11.2017 to midnight 29.11.2018)
Holdings: In the absence of documentary proof of income, deceased's income is assessed at minimum wages applicable to a matriculate on the date of accident. For a bachelor deceased with only parents and siblings as dependants, 50% deduction is made from annual income for personal expenses before calculating loss of dependency. Future prospects are not awarded where income is assessed at minimum wages and the deceased was not shown to have been in fixed salaried or self-employed work, following Laxmidhar Nayak v. Juggal Kishore Behera.
Outcome: MACT 74/18 (death claim): Rs. 12,36,660 awarded to parents and brother with 9% interest per annum from date of filing. MACT 124/18 (injury claim): Rs. 1,89,150 awarded to Sherddin with 9% interest per annum. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. held liable for both awards; amounts directed to be deposited with UCO Bank.
This common award disposed of MACT 74/18 (death claim by parents and brother of deceased Istkhar) and MACT 124/18 (injury claim by Sherddin) before the MACT, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi. On 10 February 2018 at about 5 PM, deceased Istkhar and injured Sherddin were travelling on motorcycle DL 1 SZ 1427 near village Meetlli towards Meerut when bus UP 15 AT 4990 struck their motorcycle. Istkhar died; Sherddin was injured. Crime No. 166/18 was registered at PS Baghpat under Sections 279/337/427/304-A IPC. Negligence of the bus driver was found established. For MACT 74/18 (death): Istkhar's income was assessed at minimum wages for a matriculate (Rs. 11,830 per month). As a bachelor, 50% was deducted for personal expenses. Multiplier 17 was applied for age approximately 28. No future prospects were added per Laxmidhar Nayak. Total loss of dependency was Rs. 12,06,660, with Rs. 15,000 each for loss of estate and funeral expenses—totalling Rs. 12,36,660. For MACT 124/18 (injury): Sherddin failed to prove disability as no treating doctor was summoned. Income assessed at Rs. 11,830 per month. No future income loss was awarded; total compensation was Rs. 1,89,150 covering loss of wages, pain and suffering, attendant charges, and diet. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. was found liable for both awards with 9% interest per annum from date of filing.

Legal area: motor_accident; stage: claim_petition

Stance: claimant_supporting
Facts: On 19.05.2016 at about 8 AM, deceased Sachin (motor mechanic, approximately 30 years) and injured Naresh were travelling on motorcycle DL 5 SAM 2688; offending vehicle UP 14 ET 9761 hit the motorcycle near Rajiv Colony, Karheda, Sahibabad Sachin died at Narender Mohan Hospital, Ghaziabad; Naresh was referred to GTB Hospital Delhi; Crime No. 726/16 registered at PS Sahibabad under Section 279/338/304A IPC Sachin's income assessed at minimum wages for unskilled workman (Rs. 9,568 per month as on 19.05.2016); 1/4th personal expenses deduction applied (father, Petitioner No. 4, not dependent); multiplier 17 for age 30; no future prospects (Pranay Sethi) Loss of dependency for MACT 416/16: Rs. 14,63,904; total with consortium, estate, and funeral: Rs. 15,33,904 Naresh (MACT 417/16): 33% physical disability (permanent locomotor impairment, right upper limb); functional disability assessed at 15% of the whole body following Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar (2011) 1 SCC 343; multiplier 17 for age 27; total award Rs. 4,31,478 Reliance General Insurance Co. held liable under policy No. 1302252334005367 (06.01.2016 to 05.01.2017); no policy violation found
Holdings: Negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle is established on preponderance of probability through FIR, site plan, and MLC; the respondents led no evidence in rebuttal. Where the deceased had five dependants but one (the father) was not actually dependent, the personal expenses deduction is 1/4th rather than the standard 1/3rd. Functional disability is assessed as a percentage of the whole body even though physical disability is partial; 33% limb-level disability translated to 15% whole-body functional disability following Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar (2011) 1 SCC 343.
Outcome: MACT 416/16 (death claim): Rs. 15,33,904 awarded to five petitioners (wife, two minor children, parents) with 9% interest per annum from date of filing. MACT 417/16 (injury claim): Rs. 4,31,478 awarded to Naresh with 9% interest. Reliance General Insurance Co. directed to pay both awards.

Sachin died; Naresh sustained 33% permanent locomotor impairment in his right upper limb. Crime No. 726/16 was registered under Section 279/338/304A IPC. Negligence was proved through FIR, site plan, and criminal records; the respondents produced no witness. For MACT 416/16 (death): income assessed at minimum wages for unskilled workman (Rs. 9,568 per month as of 19.05.2016). Age taken as 30 years from postmortem record. Father (Petitioner No. 4) was found not dependent, so 1/4th was deducted for personal expenses; loss of dependency was Rs. 14,63,904 (multiplier 17). Consortium (Rs. 40,000), loss of estate (Rs. 15,000), and funeral expenses (Rs. 15,000) were awarded, totalling Rs. 15,33,904. For MACT 417/16 (injury): functional disability assessed at 15% of the whole body despite 33% physical disability, following Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar (2011) 1 SCC 343. Multiplier 17 for age 27. Total compensation Rs. 4,31,478. No future prospects added per Pranay Sethi. Reliance General Insurance Co. held liable with 9% interest per annum.

Case: Mohammed Aynuddin @ Miyam vs State of Andhra Pradesh
Court: Supreme Court of India (2000)
Legal area: criminal; stage: criminal_appeal
Issues: criminal_liability, acquittal, evidence_appreciation, negligence_proof
Stance: owner_driver_supporting
Facts: On 17.12.1993 the appellant was driving an Andhra Pradesh Road Transport Corporation bus; passenger Agamma boarded the bus enroute, fell as the bus moved forward, and the rear wheel ran over her causing death All three courts below (trial court, Sessions Court, and High Court in revision) convicted the appellant under Section 304A IPC and sentenced him to three months' imprisonment The conductor (PW3) admitted only hearing the sound of the accident while the bus was in motion; the sole eyewitness (PW4) stated only that Agamma was boarding and the bus moved, causing her to fall No witness, including the conductor, stated that the driver moved the bus before getting a signal from the conductor; the driver's version was that he was unaware of the accident
Holdings: A presumption of negligence cannot be drawn merely because a passenger fell from a bus while boarding; negligence must be positively established by evidence that the driver moved the bus prematurely or without the conductor's signal. Res ipsa loquitur applies only where the nature of the accident and attending circumstances reasonably lead to the belief that in the absence of negligence the accident would not have occurred and the thing causing injury was under the management and control of the accused. Criminal negligence requires failure to exercise duty with reasonable and proper care and precaution; where no witness establishes that the driver moved without signal, the evidence is insufficient to convict under Section 304A IPC.
Outcome: Appeal allowed. Conviction and sentence under Section 304A IPC set aside. Appellant acquitted. The Supreme Court held that the evidence was too scanty to establish criminal negligence and that res ipsa loquitur did not apply because the accident could have had multiple explanations other than negligent driving.
This 2000 Supreme Court criminal appeal concerned the conviction of an APSRTC bus driver under Section 304A of the Indian Penal Code. On 17 December 1993, passenger Agamma boarded the appellant's bus enroute; as the bus moved forward she fell and the rear wheel ran over her, causing death. The trial court, Sessions Court, and High Court in revision all convicted the driver and sentenced him to three months' imprisonment. The Supreme Court (per Thomas, J.) allowed the appeal and set aside the conviction. The court held that criminal negligence cannot be presumed merely because a passenger fell from a boarding bus; the prosecution must establish positively that the driver moved the bus prematurely or without the conductor's signal to proceed. The doctrine of res ipsa loquitur applies only where the accident cannot be reasonably attributed to causes other than negligence within the accused's control; on the present facts, a passenger's fall while boarding admits of multiple explanations. No witness, including the conductor (PW3), said the driver moved the bus before getting the signal, and the sole eyewitness (PW4) only observed the fall itself. Finding the evidence too scanty to establish criminal negligence, the Supreme Court acquitted the appellant. The judgment provides important guidance on the higher standard of evidence required for criminal liability as distinct from civil negligence.

Case: Shivlal and Ors vs Smt. Rukmabai and Ors
Court: High Court of Madhya Pradesh (1985)
Legal area: motor_accident; stage: appeal
Issues: negligence_proof, insurance_liability, policy_breach, third_party_liability, compensation_quantum, loss_of_dependency, just_compensation
Vehicles: tractor
Stance: insurer_supporting, adverse_to_claimant
Facts: On 24.04.1977 at about 11:30 AM, tractor MPU 5571 owned by Shivlal and Kanhaiyalal and driven by Shivlal turned turtle on the road between Bibdod and Ratlam near a culvert from Sagod Laxminarayan (agriculturist and milk vendor, aged about 50 years), who was travelling in the tractor brought to his field for boring of a well, died instantly in the accident Widow Rukmabai and minor sons Radheshyam and Jagdish filed Claim Case No. 16 of 1977 before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ratlam MACT awarded Rs. 32,000 to the claimants (annual dependency Rs. 2,000 with 15% deduction for lump-sum payment); owners' and insurer's appeals and claimants' cross-objections pending Owners contended deceased had forcibly occupied a seat; insurer denied liability on the ground that its policy did not cover risk of gratuitous passenger in a goods vehicle (tractor)
Holdings: A heavy vehicle (tractor) turning turtle without explanation attracts the maxim res ipsa loquitur; in the absence of credible rebuttal evidence, the presumption of negligence stands established. Under Section 95(2) of the Motor Vehicles Act the insurer's liability is limited to the statutory minimum; a policy insuring a goods vehicle (tractor) is not required to cover risk to passengers who are not carried for hire or reward. A gratuitous passenger in a goods vehicle is not covered under Section 95 of the Act; in the absence of policy terms covering such a passenger's risk, no liability can be fastened on the insurer.
Outcome: MA 26/81 (owners' appeal) dismissed: negligence of Shivlal established under res ipsa loquitur; tractor turning turtle without credible explanation raises a rebuttable presumption of negligent driving. MA 55/81 (insurer's appeal) allowed: insurer held NOT liable for gratuitous passenger not covered under Section 95 of the Motor Vehicles Act; award set aside as against insurer. Claimants' cross-objection for enhancement dismissed: Rs. 32,000 award held adequate.
This 1985 Madhya Pradesh High Court judgment decided two appeals and cross-objections against a 1980 MACT Ratlam award in Claim Case No. 16 of 1977. On 24 April 1977, tractor MPU 5571 owned by Shivlal and Kanhaiyalal turned turtle on the Bibdod-Ratlam road, killing Laxminarayan (an agriculturist and milk vendor, aged about 50), who was travelling in the tractor brought to his field for boring of a well. The MACT awarded Rs. 32,000 to his widow Rukmabai and minor sons based on annual dependency of Rs. 2,000 with a 15% deduction for lump-sum payment. The owners appealed against liability (MA 26/81) and the insurer appealed against its liability (MA 55/81); the claimants cross-objected for enhancement. The court dismissed the owners' appeal: a tractor turning turtle without credible explanation attracted res ipsa loquitur, and neither the owners' witnesses nor any plausible alternative explanation rebutted the presumption of negligence. The insurer's appeal was allowed: applying Section 95(2) of the Motor Vehicles Act and the Supreme Court's decision in Pushpabai's case (AIR 1977 SC 1735), the court held that a goods vehicle (tractor) policy is not required to cover risk to gratuitous passengers; since the policy contained no such term, no liability could be fastened on the insurer. The claimants' cross-objection was dismissed, the Tribunal's Rs. 32,000 award being found adequate.

Case: State of H.P. vs. Krishan Lal
Court: High Court of Himachal Pradesh, Shimla (2024)
Legal area: criminal; stage: criminal_appeal
Issues: rash_negligent_driving, negligence_proof, evidence_appreciation, acquittal, fir_credibility
Vehicles: private_vehicle
Stance: neutral
Facts: On 30.08.2006 a vehicle bearing registration No. HP-01A-3243 driven by accused Krishan Lal alias Babli fell into a gorge at place Thachi due to alleged high speed and negligence. Three persons (Yog Raj, Paras Ram and Besar Dutt) died on the spot; other occupants including Mohan Lal, Virender and Sanju sustained injuries. The accused denied rash driving and claimed the accident occurred because the retaining wall (danga) on the road suddenly gave way. Trial Court acquitted the accused under Sections 279, 337, 338 and 304-A IPC after finding the retaining wall collapse version plausible, supported by prosecution witnesses' own cross-examination admissions. The State filed Cr. Appeal No. 189 of 2011 against the judgment of acquittal dated 31.07.2010.
Holdings: When two views are possible from evidence in a criminal case, the one in favour of the accused must be accepted; the prosecution must prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Use of the term 'high speed' by lay witnesses is legally insufficient to establish rashness or negligence without ascertaining what the witness understood by that expression. A witness may not depose as to whether a driver was negligent; negligence is an inference to be drawn by the court from proven facts. An appellate court will not interfere with an order of acquittal unless the Trial Court's view is perverse, illegal or affected by an error of law or fact.
Outcome: Criminal appeal by State of H.P. dismissed. Acquittal of accused Krishan Lal upheld. High Court held the Trial Court's view was a plausible and reasonable view based on material on record, as prosecution witnesses admitted in cross-examination that the danga (retaining wall) on the road had collapsed, raising a reasonable alternative explanation. The accused was ordered released from custody.
The State of Himachal Pradesh appealed against the acquittal of Krishan Lal alias Babli, who was charged under Sections 279, 337, 338 and 304-A IPC and Section 186 MV Act arising from a road accident on 30.08.2006 in which a vehicle fell into a gorge killing three persons and injuring others. The accused claimed the accident resulted from the sudden collapse of a retaining wall. The Trial Court acquitted him after prosecution witnesses themselves admitted in cross-examination that the 'danga' on the road gave way, the vehicle was not driven at high speed in rainy conditions, and the retaining wall had collapsed. The High Court, applying the parameters in Mallappa v. State of Karnataka, held that when two equally plausible views emerge from evidence the one favourable to the accused must be adopted. Witness statements that the accused was driving negligently were held inadmissible as expressions of opinion rather than depositions of fact. Bare reference to 'high speed' without any attempt to quantify or explain the term was held legally insufficient. The appeal was dismissed and the accused ordered released.

Case: Chaina Ram vs. State of H.P.
Court: High Court of Himachal Pradesh, Shimla (2025)
Legal area: criminal; stage: revision
Issues: rash_negligent_driving, negligence_proof, driving_license_validity, conviction, evidence_appreciation
Vehicles: bus
Stance: owner_driver_supporting, neutral
Facts: On 11.03.2003, victim Akshay Kumar (PW-2) was boarding bus HP53-2713 at the old bus stand in Palampur when driver Chaina Ram started the bus. Akshay Kumar fell and his left leg was crushed under the rear tyre of the bus, sustaining simple and grievous injuries. Trial Court convicted accused under Sections 279, 337, 338 IPC and Section 181 MV Act; Appellate Court affirmed conviction. In revision before the High Court, the accused argued no evidence showed he moved the bus without conductor's signal, and that absence of driving license does not constitute negligence. Accused never produced any driving license before the Trial Court, Appellate Court, or High Court.
Holdings: To fasten criminal liability on a bus driver for negligent driving when a passenger falls while boarding, there must be evidence that the driver moved the bus without getting a signal from the conductor. Absence of a driving license does not per se constitute rashness or negligence in driving; liability under Section 181 MV Act is separate from criminal negligence under IPC. No presumption of negligence can be drawn against a driver merely because a passenger fell from the bus while boarding. In revisional jurisdiction under Section 397 CrPC, the High Court does not exercise appellate jurisdiction and should not re-appreciate evidence to reverse concurrent factual findings unless there is perversity, illegality, or a gross miscarriage of justice.
Outcome: Revision partly allowed. Conviction and sentence under Sections 279, 337 and 338 IPC set aside; prosecution failed to prove accused moved the bus without receiving conductor's signal. Conviction under Section 181 MV Act upheld as accused never produced driving license before any court. Fine for Section 181 MV Act conviction maintained.
Chaina Ram, a bus driver, was convicted by the Trial Court under Sections 279, 337, 338 IPC and Section 181 MV Act after passenger Akshay Kumar's leg was crushed under the rear tyre of bus HP53-2713 while boarding at Palampur bus stand on 11.03.2003. The conviction was affirmed in appeal. In revision before the Himachal Pradesh High Court, the Court applied the law laid down by the Supreme Court in Mohd. Aynuddin v. State of A.P. and held that to impose criminal liability for negligent driving in a bus-boarding scenario, the prosecution must specifically prove that the driver moved the bus without receiving a signal from the conductor. No prosecution witness deposed to this fact. One witness (PW-9) suggested the victim was pushed by other passengers. Accordingly, the conviction under Sections 279, 337, 338 IPC was set aside for insufficient proof. However, since the accused never produced any driving license before any court despite being given the opportunity, the conviction under Section 181 MV Act was upheld. The revision was partly allowed to this limited extent.

text:
Case: Sanjay vs. State of Haryana
Court: High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh (2025)
Legal area: criminal; stage: revision
Issues: rash_negligent_driving, negligence_proof, evidence_appreciation, conviction, sentencing, fir_credibility
Vehicles: other
Stance: neutral
Facts: On 17.11.2016 at about 7:30 P.M. near Kabrel bus stand area, Hisar, a pick-up van bearing registration No. HR 44 E 0207 driven rashly and negligently by Sanjay struck Balbir who was near the khokha of Vikas on the roadside. The offending vehicle also rammed into the khokha of PW-7 Vikas, causing property damage. Sanjay fled the spot. Balbir succumbed to injuries on 09.12.2016 after continuous treatment at multiple hospitals; Section 304-A IPC was added. Accused Sanjay was identified in court by eyewitnesses PW-6 Satish (son of deceased) and PW-7 Vikas; no Test Identification Parade was held. Trial Court convicted and sentenced the accused; Additional Sessions Judge dismissed the criminal appeal. The offending vehicle was not insured.
Holdings: Continuous shifting of an injured person from one hospital to another does not break the causal nexus between the accident and death; the family cannot be attributed negligence for such transfers absent positive medical evidence of improper treatment. Identification of an accused in court by natural witnesses who had adequate opportunity to observe the accused is valid even without a prior Test Identification Parade. The doctrine of res ipsa loquitur applies where a vehicle crosses the entire width of a road and strikes a pedestrian standing off the road; no contributory negligence can be attributed to such a pedestrian. Compensation awarded in a civil motor accident claim is a relevant mitigating factor while considering modification of sentence in a criminal revision.
Outcome: Revision petition partly allowed on sentence only. Conviction under all sections affirmed. Sentence under Section 304-A IPC reduced from 2 years rigorous imprisonment to 18 months rigorous imprisonment, considering petitioner is aged 44 years, is the sole breadwinner with four minor children and a deceased wife, and civil compensation of Rs. 11,76,509 has already been awarded under Section 166 MV Act. All other sentences and fine unchanged.
Sanjay, the registered owner and driver of pick-up van HR 44 E 0207, was convicted by the Trial Court under Sections 279, 337, 304-A, 427 IPC and Sections 181 and 192 MV Act for rashly driving and causing the death of Balbir on 17.11.2016 near Kabrel bus stand, Hisar. The Additional Sessions Judge dismissed the criminal appeal. In the criminal revision before the Punjab and Haryana High Court, the petitioner challenged the conviction on three grounds: the causal chain was broken by repeated hospital transfers, in-court identification without TIP was unreliable, and the sentence was excessive. The High Court rejected all contentions on conviction. It held that continuous medical treatment linked the death to the accident, and no medical evidence suggested improper treatment or a break in causation. Identification by natural witnesses PW-6 and PW-7, who had opportunity to observe the accused and were not impeached in cross-examination, was held valid without TIP. The site plan demonstrating that the pick-up van crossed the entire road to strike a pedestrian standing off the road established res ipsa loquitur. On sentence, the Court granted partial relief under Section 304-A, reducing imprisonment from two years to eighteen months RI, considering the petitioner's age, family circumstances (sole breadwinner, four minor children), and the civil compensation already awarded.

text:
Case: The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Smt. Rani And Others
Court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench (2019)
Legal area: motor_accident; stage: appeal
Issues: compensation_quantum, contributory_negligence, insurance_liability, multiplier, loss_of_dependency, section_166
Vehicles: motorcycle, other
Stance: claimant_supporting, adverse_to_insurer
Facts: On 22.06.2009 at about 3:00 p.m. deceased Ramhet was riding Motorcycle No. UP 42-G/2180 from village Umaradeeh to Jamo with father-in-law Shyam Lal and mother-in-law Dhanpata Devi as pillion riders. Mini Truck No. 44 AH/4081 driven rashly and negligently by Ram Sumer collided with the motorcycle from the front side near Dharmshala of Jivnanandan Tiwari Ka Purwa; Ramhet died on the spot and pillion riders sustained severe injuries. FIR No. 375/2009 was registered under Sections 338, 279, 427, 304-A IPC at Police Station Jamo, District Sultanpur. MACT Sultanpur (MACP No. 232 of 2009) awarded Rs. 4,17,500 with 7% interest using multiplier 17 and notional income Rs. 3,000 per month for the 32-year-old deceased. Oriental Insurance Company (insurer of the offending truck) filed FAFO No. 757 of 2011 challenging the award on grounds of excessive compensation, contributory negligence, and wrongful rejection of Section 170 application.
Holdings: In motor accident claims the standard of proof is preponderance of probability, not proof beyond reasonable doubt; the Tribunal is not a criminal court. Where the insurer is already impleaded as a party respondent in the claim petition, it can contest on all available grounds without restriction to statutory defences under Section 149(2); a separate Section 170 application is unnecessary. Contributory negligence must be proved by documentary or oral evidence; an unsubstantiated plea of negligence for carrying two pillion riders will fail in absence of such evidence. An insurer of the offending vehicle is responsible to indemnify the third party where the insurance coverage was effective at the relevant date of accident.
Outcome: Appeal dismissed. MACT award of Rs. 4,17,500 with interest at 7% per annum confirmed. Insurer directed to pay entire compensation within one month from date of judgment.
The Oriental Insurance Company appealed against a MACT Sultanpur award of Rs. 4,17,500 at 7% interest, arising from the death of Ramhet whose motorcycle UP 42-G/2180 was hit from the front by Mini Truck No. 44 AH/4081 on 22.06.2009. The insurer argued the award was excessive, the deceased was contributorily negligent in carrying two pillion riders, the Section 170 application was wrongly rejected, and the driver was not examined. The Allahabad High Court held: (i) in MACT proceedings the standard is preponderance of probability, not proof beyond reasonable doubt, making the claim valid; (ii) the insurer produced no documentary or oral evidence to rebut eyewitness PW-2 Shyam Lal's account that the truck driver was on the wrong side; (iii) since the insurer was already impleaded as opposite party respondent, it was entitled to contest on all grounds and the Section 170 application was unnecessary; and (iv) the multiplier of 17 for age 32 and notional income Rs. 3,000 per month were in accord with Schedule Table of Section 163(A). The appeal was dismissed and the award confirmed.

text:
Case: Surendra Singh And Another vs. Vijay Singh And Another (with connected appeals)
Court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (2018)
Legal area: motor_accident; stage: appeal
Issues: compensation_quantum, compensation_enhancement, multiplier, future_prospects, loss_of_dependency, just_compensation, section_166
Vehicles: truck, car
Stance: claimant_supporting
Facts: Four connected First Appeals from Orders all involved death of bachelor sons (ages 16, 27, 23 and 20) caused in separate motor vehicle accidents, with parents claiming compensation. In FAFO 3484/2012: Kapil Singh (16 years) was hit by truck UP-78 BT-3985 on 22.07.2010; Tribunal applied multiplier 7 based on age of claimant parents, not the deceased. In FAFO 1199/2016: Rakesh Kumar (27 years) died on 29.11.2003; Tribunal applied multiplier 11 based on parents' age instead of deceased's age, and denied future prospects. In FAFO 1820/2002: Pankaj Agarwal (23 years) died on 08.09.1997; Tribunal applied multiplier 15 but did not award future prospects for fixed salary employee. In FAFO 4230/2017: Dharmendra (20 years) died on 17.09.2010; Reliance Insurance appealed the award claiming higher deduction for personal expenses, but the correct multiplier (18) with future prospects results in higher total compensation. After the judgment reserved on 21.09.2017, the Supreme Court's constitution bench in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi was pronounced on 31.10.2017; the case was re-listed and decided thereafter.
Holdings: The multiplier for computing compensation in motor accident death cases must be applied with reference to the age of the deceased (using the Sarla Verma table as approved in Pranay Sethi), not the age of the claimant parent. Future prospects must be awarded for self-employed persons and persons on fixed salary: 40% if deceased was below 40 years, 25% if between 40-50 years, and 10% if between 50-60 years. Future prospects cannot be awarded on notional income, since notional income is never actually earned and cannot constitute 'established income' within the meaning of Pranay Sethi. In non-adversarial MACT proceedings, a court can enhance compensation in an insurer's appeal without cross-objection by the claimants, by applying the correct legal principle laid down by the Supreme Court, under Order XLI Rule 33 CPC.
Outcome: FAFO Nos. 3484/2012, 1199/2016 and 1820/2002 (claimant appeals) allowed with substantially enhanced compensation. FAFO No. 4230/2017 (insurer appeal) also allowed on the ground of higher personal expense deduction (1/2 for bachelor), but total compensation enhanced to Rs. 5,83,500/- because the correct multiplier of 18 and 40% future prospects together yielded a higher overall figure.
Four First Appeals from Orders were consolidated before the Allahabad High Court to resolve common questions of law: the correct multiplier in bachelor death cases and entitlement to future prospects for the self-employed and fixed salary deceased. Judgment was reserved in September 2017 but the matter was re-opened after the Supreme Court's Constitution Bench decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (31.10.2017). The Court held: (i) the multiplier must be applied with reference to the age of the deceased, following the Sarla Verma table as approved in Pranay Sethi, and not the age of the parent-claimant; (ii) future prospects at 40% must be added to established income of self-employed and fixed-salary deceased below 40 years; (iii) future prospects cannot be awarded where income is notional, not established; (iv) standardized non-pecuniary heads from Pranay Sethi (loss of estate Rs. 15,000, consortium Rs. 40,000, funeral Rs. 15,000 enhanced at 10% every 3 years) apply. All three claimant appeals were allowed with substantially enhanced awards. The insurer's appeal on personal expense deduction was also allowed but the net effect was a higher total award. The Court exercised its power under Order XLI Rule 33 CPC to enhance even in the insurer's appeal.

text:
Case: Yogeshkumar Badharsinh Baria vs. Dilipkumar Ranchhodbhai Damor And Another
Court: High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad (2025)
Legal area: motor_accident; stage: appeal
Issues: compensation_quantum, compensation_enhancement, future_prospects, income_determination, multiplier, just_compensation, section_166
Vehicles: other
Stance: claimant_supporting
Facts: Original claimant Yogeshkumar Badharsinh Baria sustained amputation of right leg below knee in a motor accident caused by rash and negligent driving of respondent no. 1. Claimant was 28 years old at time of accident and was engaged as a skilled worker in masonry and centering work; also earned from agriculture. MACT (Auxiliary) & 6th Additional District Judge, Panchmahals at Godhra awarded Rs. 4,68,600 in MACP No. 695 of 2016 (judgment dated 08.02.2023). Disability certificates showed 65% permanent disability (doctor opined 70% but conceded 35% as whole body disability in cross-examination); Tribunal applied 35% disability. Tribunal also assessed income at Rs. 4,000 per month instead of minimum wages rate of Rs. 7,800 per month applicable to skilled workers for April-September 2016 period.
Holdings: Functional disability for amputation below knee must be assessed at 50% per Schedule I Part II of the Employees Compensation Act 1923 (Entry Nos. 20 and 21), which is the percentage of loss of earning capacity for such specific injury, particularly when the claimant's occupation requires physical mobility. Income of a skilled worker should be assessed with reference to the prescribed minimum wages; for April-September 2016 the applicable rate was Rs. 7,800 per month. Courts should not adopt a stereotypical or myopic approach in assessing disabilities and compensation; the functional impact of the injury on the claimant's earning capacity in their specific occupation is the relevant measure. Future medical expenses including the cost of prosthetic limb and its periodic replacement must be awarded as a separate head; failure by the Tribunal to consider this is a material error.
Outcome: Appeal allowed. Total compensation revised from Rs. 4,68,600 to Rs. 16,42,440 (enhanced by Rs. 11,73,840), with interest at 9% p.a. from date of filing of claim petition till actual realization. Respondents held jointly and severally liable. Enhanced amount to be deposited with concerned Tribunal within eight weeks.
Original claimant Yogeshkumar Badharsinh Baria, a 28-year-old skilled worker engaged in masonry and centering, suffered amputation of right leg below the knee in a motor accident. The MACT Godhra awarded Rs. 4,68,600 in MACP No. 695 of 2016, applying 35% whole body disability and income of Rs. 4,000 per month, and omitting future medical expenses. On appeal before the Gujarat High Court, the Court held: (i) functional disability for amputation below knee should be 50% per Schedule I Part II ECA 1923, Entries 20 and 21, especially for a masonry worker requiring full physical mobility; (ii) income must be assessed at minimum wages for skilled workers, being Rs. 7,800 per month for the relevant period April-September 2016; (iii) future prospects at 40% are applicable per Pranay Sethi as the claimant was below 40; (iv) multiplier 17 for age 28 confirmed; (v) future medical expenses including prosthetic limb Rs. 2,50,000 must be separately awarded. Applying monthly income Rs. 7,800, 40% future prospects (Rs. 10,920/month), 50% disability (Rs. 5,460/month), multiplier 17, the future loss of income was Rs. 11,13,840. Adding enhanced pain/suffering Rs. 1,00,000, SAT Rs. 25,000, medical Rs. 60,000, actual loss Rs. 93,600, and future medical Rs. 2,50,000, total compensation was enhanced to Rs. 16,42,440.

Case: Rajesh Kumar Shukla And Another vs. Naseem Ahmed And Others (with connected petitions)
Court: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Pilot Court), Karkardooma Courts, Delhi (2018)
Legal area: motor_accident; stage: claim_petition
Issues: rash_negligent_driving, compensation_quantum, loss_of_dependency, insurance_liability, section_166, third_party_liability, interest_on_compensation
Vehicles: truck, car
Stance: claimant_supporting
Facts: On 09.06.2015 at about 5:45 hrs, the family was travelling in Wagon-R No. DL 2 CAL 3562 on NH 24 from Delhi to Faizabad, UP. At Village Kotra, PS Praswa, Sub Division Mohamdi, Lakhimpur Kheri, a speeding truck No. UP 27 5376 owned by M/s Sparsh Transport Carrier Pvt. Ltd. and driven by Naseem Ahmed came from the opposite direction in high speed and in gross violation of lane driving and hit the Wagon-R. Shaksham Shukla (approximately 5 years old, DOB 17.10.2010) sustained fatal injuries and died; Anushka Shukla (6 years) sustained head injuries with 7 stitches; Meena Shukla (29 years) sustained rib fractures and head injuries; Vansh Shukla (9 months) sustained head injuries and right upper limb weakness. FIR No. 16/15 registered under Sections 279/337/338/304A/427 IPC at PS Praswa. Respondent No. 3 (United India Insurance Co. Ltd.) confirmed policy No. 0805013114P107786597 was valid from 31.12.2014 to 30.12.2015.
Holdings: In motor accident claims, FIR, chargesheet and eyewitness testimony on the standard of preponderance of probability are sufficient to establish negligence of the offending vehicle driver. For death of a child in a motor accident where no established income exists, compensation is computed using inflation-corrected notional income (Rs. 15,000 p.a. from Second Schedule, multiplied by CII for year of accident divided by base CII 331), deducting 1/3 for personal expenses, applying appropriate multiplier, and adding equal amount for composite non-pecuniary damages. An insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation when the insurance policy was valid at the time of accident and no violation of policy terms is proved. Loss of wages of an employed person during treatment period and actual medical expenses are separate and cognizable heads of compensation.
Outcome: All four claim petitions allowed. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. directed to pay: Rs. 6,53,334 with 9% interest from date of filing (MACT 14615/15 - death of Shaksham Shukla); Rs. 88,663 with 9% interest (MACT 15128/15 - injuries to Anushka Shukla); Rs. 1,83,444 with 9% interest (MACT 15129/15 - injuries to Meena Shukla); Rs. 26,172 with 9% interest (MACT 15182/15 - injuries to Vansh Shukla).
Four connected MACT petitions filed by members of the Shukla family arising from a road accident on 09.06.2015 on NH 24 at Lakhimpur Kheri when speeding truck UP 27 5376, owned by M/s Sparsh Transport Carrier Pvt. Ltd. and driven by Naseem Ahmed, collided with their Wagon-R car DL 2 CAL 3562. Shaksham Shukla (age 5 years) died of fatal injuries; Anushka Shukla (6 yrs, head injuries), Meena Shukla (29 yrs, rib fractures), and Vansh Shukla (9 months, head injuries) survived with varying injuries. The Tribunal applied the preponderance of probability standard and found negligence established through criminal records, eyewitness testimony, and adverse inference from the driver's non-appearance in the witness box. For Shaksham's death, the Delhi High Court's formula for child deaths was applied: notional income Rs. 15,000 p.a. (Second Schedule) inflation-corrected using CII 1081/331 = Rs. 49,000 p.a.; deducting 1/3 personal expenses gives Rs. 32,666; multiplier 10 for child below 5 years gives pecuniary loss Rs. 3,26,667; adding equal amount for composite non-pecuniary damages, total = Rs. 6,53,334. United India Insurance Co. Ltd., confirmed as insurer with valid policy, was held liable for all amounts across the four petitions.
